stories.headline: Three scientists share the Nobel Prize in Medicine for optogenetics
stories.summary: The Nobel Assembly at Karolinska Institutet announced the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine on 5 October 2026. It went to Karl Deisseroth of Stanford University and to the German scientists Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel, for their discoveries concerning light-gated ion channels and optogenetics. Deisseroth gave the field its name in 2006.

stories.headline: Quebec's governing party loses all its seats as the Parti Québécois wins
stories.summary: Quebec voted on 5 October 2026 to elect the members of its National Assembly. The governing Coalition Avenir Québec, led by Premier Christine Fréchette, lost all 79 of the seats it held. The Parti Québécois won for the first time since 2012, and its leader, Paul St-Pierre Plamondon, is set to become the 34th Premier of Quebec at the head of a minority government.

stories.headline: Spain will hold a snap general election in November
stories.summary: Spain's parliament voted down two emergency housing decrees, which would have restricted evictions and frozen rents. The prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, then called a snap general election for 29 November 2026. All 350 seats in the Congress of Deputies and 209 of the 267 seats in the Senate will be contested.

stories.headline: NASA backs a hunt for a cave under a lunar pit
stories.summary: NASA has chosen a proposal led by the Planetary Science Institute to find out whether a large cave stretches underground from the opening of a pit on the Moon. The project, called GIMLI, will study the Marius Hill Pit, a large opening in one of the Moon's most volcanically varied regions. The Norwegian Space Agency will provide the ground-penetrating radar.

The 2026 Quebec general election was held on October 5, 2026, to elect members to the National Assembly of the 44th Quebec Legislature. Lieutenant Governor Manon Jeannotte dropped the writs of election on August 27, 2026, after Premier Christine Fréchette advised her to dissolve the legislature.

Frechette would lead the governing Coalition Avenir Québec to a historic defeat, losing all 79 of their seats in the election. Plamondon would lead the Parti Quebecois to victory for the first time since 2012, and is set to become the 34th Premier of Quebec.
The Parti Québécois lost most of its remaining seats but managed to elect its previously seatless leader Paul St-Pierre Plamondon to a seat.
